title: What if a black hole appeared in your pocket?

hook.narration: A black hole just appeared in your pocket.

scenes.narration: That little circle weighs about as much as the whole Earth.
fact_sources: Schwarzschild radius r_s = 2GM/c^2: a 1 cm-radius black hole has mass ~6.7e24 kg, i.e. roughly one Earth mass (order-of-magnitude)

scenes.narration: It falls through your hand, through the floor, through the sidewalk.
fact_sources: geometry: event horizon radius ~1e-13 m vs atom ~1e-10 m — the hole passes through matter like a ghost, gravity does the damage

scenes.narration: Matter is mostly empty space. To this thing, solid rock is a rumor.
fact_sources: standard atomic-structure fact: nucleus is ~1/100,000 of the atom radius

scenes.narration: It loops the planet through the core, and every pass cracks the crust.
fact_sources: classic gravitation result: an object dropped through Earth oscillates through the core; tidal stresses follow it

scenes.narration: And no, it doesn't swallow the Earth in one bite. Real black holes eat slowly: atom by atom, patient, invisible.
fact_sources: micro black-hole accretion is extremely slow (tiny capture cross-section) — CERN LSAG safety review conclusions

scenes.narration: But patience wins. One day the ground gives up, and the planet folds itself into a marble.
fact_sources: Earth's own Schwarzschild radius is ~8.9 mm — the whole planet compressed to marble size

scenes.narration: Check your pocket. The universe already did.

loop_line: Check your pocket. The universe already did.
